subject: Math
skill: Evaluating Statistical Claims Observational Studies And Experiments
prompt: A researcher studying sleep patterns recruited $60$ volunteers from among employees at a technology company to participate in an experiment. The volunteers were randomly assigned to either use a sleep-tracking device or not use the device for $30$ days. At the end of the study, the researcher found that volunteers who used the sleep-tracking device reported significantly better sleep quality than those who did not use the device. To which of the following groups can the results of this experiment be appropriately generalized?

choices.B: All adults who have sleep problems
choices.C: All employees at this specific technology company
choices.D: The $60$ volunteers who participated in the experiment

explanation: The volunteers were recruited from employees at one technology company, not randomly selected from any broader population. While random assignment allows the researcher to establish a causal relationship for these $60$ volunteers, the results can only be generalized to the volunteers who actually participated in the study, not to any broader group.
